title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC0RA_0LD0LB_1RD1LE_0RC0RA_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC0RA_0LD0LB_1RD1LE_0RC0RA_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A long bouncer over a 1010… background growing to the right (fastest of the batch), with a nearly frozen left end that is reached rarely and grows by single cells; defects (00, 11) sit in the background; open.

Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone), 12 shift rules of the sweeps; the rest of the description below is observation of the run, marked as such.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 143,859 cells have been visited and 71,897 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 9.30×10<sup>17</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 930,714,372,877,348,461 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,000,349 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.254). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.607).

claims.title: 12 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: A, B and F shift 10↔01 rightward; B and C cross leftward unchanged. Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (F reading 1) needs 01001, 0101x or 01010 to the left and a right side starting 10. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer over a 10 background with a defect gas
claims.text: The tape is nearly all 10. Every pass shifts the background by one cell (six proved shift rules in both phases). The right end grows like t0.6 (88,047 cells after 109 steps), faster than a plain √t bouncer: most passes do not reach the left end at all.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 143,859 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

facts.value: bouncer over a 10 background with a defect gas

sections.heading: What the machine does: bouncer over a 10 background with a defect gas
html: The tape is nearly all 10. Every pass shifts the background by one cell (six proved shift rules in both phases). The right end grows like t0.6 (88,047 cells after 109 steps), faster than a plain √t bouncer: most passes do not reach the left end at all.

The left end is reached rarely and moves only 153 cells in 109 steps; at those visits the left edge reads : 1 : 1 . 1 . 1 … or . 1 . 1 … (a double gap or none), and isolated defects (00, 11, 000) sit in the background, e.g. … 1 0^2 1 0 1 0^2 1 0 1 … 1 0^3 1 0^2 1 0 1 … near the right end at step 9,264.
So the head turns somewhere inside the tape most of the time; the turning points are set by the defects. We have not found the rule that decides where a pass turns.

sections.heading: What a halt would require
html: F reading 1 halts; in the 5-cell closed language with 0101x/01001 on the left and 10… on the right.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html:
• Sweeps (lean/Sweeps.lean, kernel): A, B and F shift 10↔01 rightward; B and C cross leftward unchanged; for every number of copies and every tape around.
  • Bounded run (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in 107 steps (native), 10,000 (kernel); the halting transition is the only way to stop.
Everything else on this page is observation of the simulated run (heuristic). Nothing here decides halting.

sections.heading: What would move it forward
html: Record the turning points of the passes and the defect positions; the t0.6 growth suggests passes of geometrically distributed length.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.254). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.607).
After 109 steps the tape spans 143,859 cells (153 left of the start, 88,047 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
